quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, filed 08-14-2026, consolidated): H1 revenue KRW 41,274M vs KRW 9,483M in H1 2025; H1 operating profit KRW 2,169M vs an operating loss of KRW 8,587M. Q2 alone: revenue KRW 31,469M (Q2 2025: KRW 7,567M), operating profit KRW 4,135M (Q2 2025: loss of KRW 2,880M). H1 net profit KRW 8,521M included an equity-method gain of KRW 3,797M, mostly from affiliate SEMCNS. Product mix: memory testers including burn-in and CLT KRW 37,600M (91.1%), SSD testers KRW 3,674M (8.9%), SoC testers nil; domestic sales KRW 39,189M (94.9%), with India KRW 1,471,215 thousand.

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog (disclosed orders): KRW 101,801M ordered, KRW 17,203M delivered, KRW 84,598M outstanding -- CLT and related testers KRW 30,200M (ordered 2026-02-27, due 2026-12-31, KRW 14,200M outstanding), CIB boards KRW 9,686M (due 2026-09-04, KRW 8,483M outstanding), CIB and others KRW 12,065M (due 2026-12-31) and SSD testers and others KRW 49,850M (ordered 2026-07-07, due 2026-12-31). quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and utilisation, H1 2026: capacity of 84 memory-tester systems and 3,750 board sets (3,834 units in total); production of 11 CLT and other systems plus 1,830 boards (1,841 units), an average utilisation of 48.0%. Unrecognised commitments to acquire property and intangible assets totalled KRW 8,861M at 06-30-2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilisation 48.0% (1,841 of 3,834 units); capex commitments KRW 8,861M

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration: a single unnamed customer ('major customer 1') accounted for KRW 39,596,206 thousand of KRW 41,274,152 thousand revenue in H1 2026 (H1 2025: KRW 8,579,724 thousand of KRW 9,482,920 thousand). All four supply contracts disclosed in the report are with Samsung Electronics.
quarterly_data.figure: Major customer 1 KRW 39,596,206 thousand of KRW 41,274,152 thousand H1 revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Products and R&D: the chamber-type low-frequency tester (CLT), developed at a customer's request, has been supplied to new DRAM mass-production lines since 2025; it tests 11,520 DRAM components simultaneously at -20 to 150 degrees C. In development: CLT interface boards for GDDR and HBM, a cold-chamber NAND burn-in tester, DDI and AP testers, and next-generation DDR6 test technology. Development is complete on PCIe Gen6 / SAS 64G SSD testers and a CXL 3.1 tester; the company expects the CXL test market to expand at end-2026 or in H1 2027. The company is marketing to Kioxia to diversify customers. H1 2026 R&D spending KRW 9,504M before government grants (20.70% of revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: CLT tests 11,520 DRAM parts at once; R&D KRW 9,504M (20.70%)

quarterly_data.signal: Raw-material purchases, H1 2026: ICs KRW 16,358M (40.0%, Analog Devices (ADI) and others), mechanical parts KRW 2,948M (7.2%, Okins Electronics and others), PCBs KRW 3,344M (8.2%, Tiger Elec and others), cables KRW 407M (1.0%, Samtec and others); total KRW 40,873M. Related-party purchases of raw materials included YC KRW 3,198,025 thousand, YC America KRW 811,535 thousand and Oracom KRW 984,047 thousand.
